entities.summary:
John of Nepomuk 
was a saint of Bohemia. He was executed by King Wenceslaus IV of Bohemia for disobedience. John was thrown into the Vltava river.

Born around 1352, John of Nepomuk was a Bohemian cleric who rose to prominence as a spiritual leader and advocate for the poor. He was known for his piety, compassion, and unwavering dedication to the people of Bohemia.

In 1393, John of Nepomuk was arrested and put on trial by King Wenceslaus IV, who accused him of treason and disobedience. Despite his protests of innocence, John was found guilty and sentenced to death. In a tragic event that shocked the kingdom, John was thrown into the Vltava river, where he drowned. His execution marked a turning point in the tumultuous history of Bohemia, as the kingdom struggled to assert its independence in the face of encroaching European powers.

Today, John of Nepomuk is remembered as a martyr and a symbol of resistance against oppressive rule. His legacy continues to inspire Catholics and non-Catholics alike, who see him as a powerful example of faith, courage, and the enduring power of the human spirit.

The Vltava river, where John met his end, remains a sacred site in Bohemia, attracting pilgrims and visitors from around the world who come to pay their respects to the saint and to reflect on the enduring significance of his story.
